comment: Life-situation index for the passage finder. Each entry maps the questions people actually type (a funeral to preach, a wedding, anxiety, grief) to an editorially curated list of passages. The 'why' lines are navigational descriptions only; the scripture text itself is always served verbatim from the corpus and every ref is validated against the canon by tests.

passages.why: The shepherd psalm; the valley of the shadow of death.
Jesus to Martha at Lazarus's tomb: I am the resurrection and the life.
Let not your heart be troubled; in my Father's house are many mansions.
Sorrow not as others which have no hope; the dead in Christ shall rise.
Death is swallowed up in victory; O death, where is thy sting?
God shall wipe away all tears; no more death, neither sorrow.
Neither death nor life can separate us from the love of God.
Moses' prayer: teach us to number our days.
Outward man perishes, inward man renewed; an eternal weight of glory.
He will swallow up death in victory and wipe away tears.
The love chapter: charity suffereth long, and is kind.
The first marriage: bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh.
Two are better than one; a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Husbands and wives; the mystery compared to Christ and the church.
Set me as a seal upon thine heart; many waters cannot quench love.
Whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people.
Put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Be careful for nothing; the peace of God shall keep your hearts.
Take no thought for the morrow; consider the lilies.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
God is our refuge and strength; be still, and know that I am God.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee; I will uphold thee.
Peace I leave with you; let not your heart be troubled.
God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power and love.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
The whole psalm of refuge under the Almighty's shadow.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee.
Be strong and of a good courage; the LORD thy God is with thee.
What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
Not the spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind.
Perfect love casteth out fear.
Why art thou cast down, O my soul? hope thou in God.
The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.
He brought me up out of an horrible pit and set my feet upon a rock.
They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength.
His compassions fail not; they are new every morning.
Elijah under the juniper tree; God meets him in a still small voice.
The God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden.
David's confession: create in me a clean heart, O God.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive.
As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions.
Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.
Thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
No condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.
I am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake.
Seventy times seven; the parable of the unmerciful servant.
Forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.
Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another.
Love your enemies; pray for them which despitefully use you.
Recompense to no man evil for evil; overcome evil with good.
Forgive, and ye shall be forgiven; good measure, pressed down.
Joseph forgives his brothers: ye thought evil, God meant it unto good.
Slow to speak, slow to wrath; man's wrath worketh not God's righteousness.
Be ye angry, and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your wrath.
A soft answer turneth away wrath.
A fool uttereth all his mind; a wise man keepeth it in.
Cease from anger, and forsake wrath; fret not thyself.
Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases.
The prayer of faith; pray one for another, that ye may be healed.
The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing.
The centurion's faith: speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
The thorn in the flesh; my grace is sufficient for thee.
Surely he hath borne our griefs; with his stripes we are healed.
Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, thou art with me.
I go to prepare a place for you.
A building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
To live is Christ, and to die is gain.
Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints.
Whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.
I have fought a good fight; henceforth a crown of righteousness.
Turn thee unto me; for I am desolate and afflicted.
He will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
God setteth the solitary in families; a father of the fatherless.
I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands.
Whither shall I flee from thy presence? Thou art there.
Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
Thomas: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
Asaph's honest struggle; whom have I in heaven but thee?
John the Baptist's question from prison, and Jesus' answer.
And of some have compassion, making a difference.

situations.label: For temptation and struggle with sin

passages.why: God will with the temptation also make a way to escape.
Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; how sin conceives.
Jesus tempted in the wilderness answers with scripture.
Tempted like as we are, yet without sin; come boldly to the throne.
Sin shall not have dominion over you.
Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin.
Walk in the Spirit; the fruit of the Spirit.
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving.
Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
In every thing give thanks.
Rejoice in the Lord alway; with thanksgiving let your requests be known.
For his mercy endureth for ever.
Be ye thankful; singing with grace in your hearts.
Lay not up treasures upon earth; ye cannot serve God and mammon.
I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
Honour the LORD with thy substance.
God loveth a cheerful giver.
Godliness with contentment is great gain; the love of money.
Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse; prove me now herewith.
Be content with such things as ye have.
Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord.
That every man should enjoy the good of all his labour.
Establish thou the work of our hands upon us.
Commit thy works unto the LORD.
Your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
Work before the fall: to dress the garden and to keep it.
Teach them diligently unto thy children.
Train up a child in the way he should go.
Children are an heritage of the LORD.
Children and fathers; nurture and admonition of the Lord.
The unfeigned faith of a grandmother and mother passed on.
That the generation to come might know them.
The prodigal son and the father who ran.
Nicodemus: ye must be born again; God so loved the world.
Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.
By grace are ye saved through faith; not of works.
The righteousness of God by faith of Jesus Christ.
Not by works of righteousness, but according to his mercy he saved us.
The Philippian jailer: what must I do to be saved?
To them gave he power to become the sons of God.
Buried with him by baptism into death; raised to walk in newness of life.
Repent, and be baptized every one of you.
The great commission: baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, Spirit.
As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
Buried with him in baptism, risen through the faith of the operation of God.
The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us.
The words of institution, and examining oneself.
Take, eat; this is my body.
I am the bread of life.
The LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
The communion of the body and blood of Christ; one bread, one body.
Do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with thy God.
Seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, plead for the widow.
Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
The LORD executeth judgment for the oppressed.
The fast God has chosen: to loose the bands of wickedness.
Jesus' Nazareth manifesto: good tidings to the poor.
The God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing.
Thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
Tribulation worketh patience; and hope maketh not ashamed.
They shall mount up with wings as eagles.
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills.
Hope as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast.
They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Troubled on every side, yet not distressed; cast down, but not destroyed.
Run with patience the race that is set before us.
Let us not be weary in well doing; in due season we shall reap.
The trying of your faith worketh patience.
Come unto me, and I will give you rest.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; he shall direct thy paths.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.
I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go.
Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths.
This is the way, walk ye in it.
Be transformed, that ye may prove what is that good will of God.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
The birth in Bethlehem; shepherds and the angelic host.
For unto us a child is born; Wonderful, Counsellor, Prince of Peace.
Joseph's dream; thou shalt call his name JESUS.
The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.
A virgin shall conceive; Immanuel, God with us.
But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah — the ruler out of little Bethlehem.
The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared.
He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.
Mary Magdalene at the tomb; the first witness.
The gospel delivered first of all: died, buried, rose again.
Christ the firstfruits of them that slept.
Why seek ye the living among the dead?
A lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

situations.label: For Good Friday and the cross

passages.why: The suffering servant: wounded for our transgressions.
The crucifixion; it is finished.
From the mocking to the centurion's confession.
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
Obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
By whose stripes ye were healed.
One sacrifice for sins for ever.
Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake.
Bless them which persecute you; overcome evil with good.
Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial.
Fret not thyself because of evildoers; commit thy way unto the LORD.
Patience and faith in all your persecutions.
Even to your old age I am he; even to hoar hairs will I carry you.
They shall still bring forth fruit in old age.
Now also when I am old, O God, forsake me not.
The hoary head is a crown of glory.
Though our outward man perish, the inward man is renewed day by day.
So teach us to number our days.

situations.label: For a new year or new beginning

passages.why: His mercies are new every morning.
Behold, I will do a new thing.
If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.
Forgetting those things which are behind, I press toward the mark.
Teach us to number our days.
Behold, I make all things new.
